newsitem.title: FINLAND: Thin Helsinki off, tone bearish after French poll.
newsitem.headline: Thin Helsinki off, tone bearish after French poll.

text.p: Shares fell in thin Monday trade with action curbed by holidays overseas and a bearish tone set by a broadly negative market response to a socialist gain in round one of France's elections, brokers said.

Generally they anticipated a bearish week after Helsinki's recent sharp gains; although the FOX derivatives index, off 0.34 percent at 1,076, fell less sharply than the less-watched HEX general index, which was off 0.43 percent at 3,107.
Volume at 212 million markka was extremely thin by Helsinki standards.
"There is no way of knowing where London will head tomorrow, but I have feeling it could be down," one broker said: another saw caution continuing with no overnight lead from New York.
Another noted a trend for Helsinki to need overseas momentum to rise, showing only bears when domestic investors are alone.

Partek stood out in an otherwise lacklustre market, putting on one markka to 96.00 and taking a fair chunk of what action there was, as investors sustained a positive response to its plan to hive off non-core concrete business in a joint venture.
Financials were relatively lively, in for some profit-taking after recent gains and as bond and money markets were ruffled by EMU difficulties some fear a French socialist win may herald.
Nokia gave back some of Friday's sharp gains in calm trade; easing 4.00 markka to 351.
